title: Suspected poisoning or chemical exposure
summary: Protect the rescuer, call the poison centre or emergency services, and avoid unadvised remedies.
sources: WHO Basic Emergency Care: Approach to the Acutely Ill and Injured
World Health Organization — Prevention and management of poisoning
2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Chemical Exposure to the Skin
actions: Protect yourself. Do not enter an area with unknown gas, fumes, or chemical contamination without appropriate training and equipment.
For severe symptoms call emergency services. Otherwise contact the verified poison centre for the selected country and follow its instructions.
Have the substance name, amount, time, route of exposure, age, approximate weight, and symptoms ready. Keep the container or a photo of the label only when safe.

Brush off a dry chemical carefully before water unless product-specific instructions say otherwise. Remove contaminated clothing and jewellery, then irrigate exposed skin with running water for at least 15 minutes.
If unresponsive but breathing normally, use the recovery position. Start CPR if breathing is absent or abnormal.
prohibitions: Do not give milk, lemon juice, salt, activated charcoal, or a neutralizing chemical unless a poison specialist directs it.
Do not enter a contaminated space to attempt a rescue.
Give nothing by mouth to a drowsy, confused, seizing, or unresponsive person.

emergencyCall.text: Call emergency services for reduced consciousness, seizure, breathing difficulty, severe burns, or a large exposure.
